messages:
Marta: Heads-up: AcmeCorp private deploy next Tues. Need KMS onboarding checklist: where to put keyring (cust project vs our control), minimal SA bindings for the agent, audit sinks, and rotation cadence. Want envelope flow + clear audit retention.

Ryan: For security and ownership we prefer customer-hosted keyrings in their project. Pros: customer owns CMKs, audit stays in their org. Cons: cross-project impersonation required for our control plane.

Ryan: Minimal bindings I usually ask for: 
- serviceAccount:redwood-kms-agent@redwood-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com => roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the specific key
- serviceAccount:redwood-control@redwood-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com => roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator (limited to the agent SA)

Cheng: Envelope pattern: customer-managed DEKs can live in their own secret store or KMS-wrapped. We keep only encrypted blobs. CMK stays in their keyring. Our rewrap/rotate flow runs via short-lived impersonation tokens. Recommend DEK rotation per workload (default 90d) and CMK rotate annually or per incident.

Marta: Good. Two customer questions likely: (1) what audit logs to enable and who gets access? (2) cross-project impersonation risks and mitigations?

Ryan: Audit: enable Cloud Audit Logs for cloudkms.googleapis.com with ADMIN_READ and DATA_WRITE. Create a sink to their BigQuery dataset or a customer-owned GCS bucket. Also enable audit for iam.serviceAccounts.getIamPolicy and iam.serviceAccounts.setIamPolicy on the SA target so token-create events show up. Grant our ops account logs/reader on the sink if we need to ingest.

Cheng: Risks: least privilege only. Grant iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator only on the specific agent SA, not project-wide. Prefer workload-identity pools or federated short-lived creds. Add an IAM condition on the binding if customer accepts e.g. restrict by requestPrincipal or time window.

Marta: Can you paste the gcloud snippets we can include in the onboarding PR? Keep them minimal and copy-paste ready.

Ryan: Sure — examples: 
```
# grant KMS encrypt/decrypt on a key
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding my-key 
  --keyring=my-keyring --location=global 
  --member='serviceAccount:redwood-kms-agent@redwood-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com' 
  --role='roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter'

# grant token-creator scoped to the customer project (narrow if possible)
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding customer-proj 
  --member='serviceAccount:redwood-control@redwood-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com' 
  --role='roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator'

# create a sink for KMS audit logs to BigQuery
gcloud logging sinks create kms_audit_bq bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/customer-bq/datasets/audit_logs 
  --log-filter='protoPayload.serviceName="cloudkms.googleapis.com"'
```

Cheng: Add monitoring: alert on failed decrypts and unexpected cryptokeyVersion.state transitions. We had a past incident where a disabled key version caused production decrypt failures. Metric-based alert + runbook saved the day.

Marta: Action items: create onboarding PR with IAM templates, gcloud snippets, audit sink template, monitoring/alert rule, and a short risk summary about cross-project impersonation. Assign to @ryan for IAM bits and @cheng for monitoring + runbook updates. ETA EOD Thursday.

kms-bot: Deploy bot: created issue REDWOOD-4567 for "AcmeCorp private KMS onboarding" and assigned ryan, cheng, marta. https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/4567 :white_check_mark:

Ryan: Quick follow-up: automation for CMK rotation — prefer optional automated rotation controlled by a customer opt-in flag. We can emit IAM audit events and a calendar reminder if they decline automation.

Cheng: Agreed. Make sure the runbook clarifies recovery steps for accidental key disable/rotation and provides sample commands to rewrap without exposing plaintext.

Marta: Perfect. I'll draft the PR and link the issue. Thanks all :thumbsup:
